Hi Amy —

Thanks — I reviewed the questionnaire. I've attached a short vendor-side summary that maps to Art. 28/30 and a current subprocessor inventory. Key points up front:

- Processing summary: Redwood acts as a processor for model inference. We do not persist customer prompt text beyond configured retention windows; see line items 4-7 in the summary for default retention behavior and controls.
- Art. 28/30: See Redwood_Art28_30_Summary.pdf for the high-level mapping; the doc references the canonical processing categories and RKIs (responsible key instances).
- Subprocessors: subprocessor_list_202605.pdf contains names, roles, country of processing, and the transfer mechanism (SCCs or adequacy). Most infra subprocessors are US-based cloud partners; for EU-hosted Dedicated or Private deployments we can restrict processing to EU regions and avoid cross-border transfers where required.
- SCCs: We support execution of EEA SCCs with customers; SCCs.pdf is the standard we offer. For large enterprise customers we can discuss a bespoke transfer addendum.

Attachments: Redwood_Art28_30_Summary.pdf; subprocessor_list_202605.pdf

If you want specific Art.30 CSV exports, tell us which processing activities you need enumerated (e.g., auth logs, telemetry, inference logs). We can provide a sanitized export.

Happy to join the walkthrough. 

– Rishi
Principal Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Amy Carlson <amy.carlson@finsecure.com>

Rishi —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the summary. A couple follow-ups from legal & procurement:

- Can you provide an Art.30-styled CSV export of processing activities (fields we need: activity id, purpose, categories of data, recipients/subprocessors, retention period, legal basis) — a sanitized version is fine.
- Procurement needs a SOC 2 or equivalent attestation. If you can share a hosted link to the report and tell us whether you will require an NDA to view the full report that would be helpful.
- Also flagging that FinSecure prefers SCCs + encryption at rest with customer-managed keys for EU production workloads — can you confirm feasibility?

Deadline: we still aim to present to our board next Thursday so the Friday window is tight but important.

Thanks,
Amy
